title: Why is the ground floor called Floor 0?
description: Each floor number tells how many button presses reach it from the ground floor. The ground floor needs no press at all, and that count gives its number. Keeko thinks the ground floor should be floor one because counting starts from one, and the count of presses breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a floor number counts the presses from the ground floor, so the place where we start has the number zero. Watch for students who want to call the ground floor floor one.

source: The ground floor is called Floor 0. Can you see why?
video_script.why: A child learns why the ground floor has the number zero, because zero as the starting point is the base of every later floor and movement.
video_script.substitution: the book's own floors counted from the Welcome Hall by lift presses
video_script.anchor: Ruhee: the floors with the Welcome Hall on the ground line, numbered by button presses from the ground floor
video_script.wrong_answer: the ground floor should be floor one
video_script.wrong_move: starts counting the ground floor as one, as in counting objects
video_script.payoff_line: The ground floor is the starting point, so its number is zero.

final_answer.value: No button needs to be pressed to be on the ground floor, so its number is 0.
final_answer.spoken: no button is pressed on the ground floor, so its number is zero

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

hold_back: Answer: no button is pressed on the ground floor, so its number is 0
never_show: Floor 0 written on the Welcome Hall before the answer
maths_rules: A floor number is the lift presses needed to reach that floor from the ground floor.
The Food Court needs one plus press (+1); the Art Centre needs two (+2); the Toy Store needs one minus press (−1).
The ground floor needs no press at all, so its number is 0.
video_script.design: One idea: the ground floor is where counting starts, so no press is needed and its number is zero. One lift picture throughout. Keeko's doubt is broken by the count of presses.
